subject: Dedicated capacity sizing and activation sequencing for PulseBridge
messages:
From: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@pulsebridge.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing and activation sequencing for PulseBridge

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Were moving this to procurement and need concrete sizing + activation options to include in the SOW. High level: our initial production workload is a conversational assistant that will peak around 75 p99 requests/minute in month 1 and we expect steady growth to ~400 p99 requests/minute by month 6. Typical prompt + response averages 800 tokens (prompt 300 / response 500).

Questions we need from Redwood for the SOW:
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs and what that buys (throughput / p99 latency targets)
- Ramp schedule (weeks/months) with clear activation triggers
- Pricing guidance for reserved capacity vs burst/overage
- Warm-up runbooks / credits for model caching and KV warm-starts

Can you propose 2-3 options (conservative, standard, aggressive) with inline tradeoffs? Procurement also asked for lead time for activation and any escrow or SLA language we should expect.

Eliza (cc) is managing the legal/procurement side from our end. Procurement email is procure@pulsebridge.ai.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Michael
VP Engineering, PulseBridge

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@pulsebridge.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing and activation sequencing for PulseBridge

Michael,

Thanks for the request and the traffic profile — thats really helpful. Ill loop Ben and Laura into a quick sizing sketch and well give you three concrete scenarios with activation timing and a recommended SLA/PO template. At a glance, the 800-token average means GPU throughput will be token-bound rather than sequence-length bound, so our proposals will include quantization and batching knobs to optimize cost.

Well aim to get a PDF + a companion forecast spreadsheet to you by EOD tomorrow (your timezone). Two quick clarifying Qs that will change the min-GPU calc:
1) Expected percentage of streaming responses vs full-completion (streaming reduces effective latency targets; any idea?)
2) Are there heavy multimodal requests (images/attachments) or is this text-only?

If you prefer, we can set a 30-min call later today to run numbers live.

-Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@pulsebridge.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: PulseBridge - Dedicated reservation options (draft)

Hi Michael / team,

Attached is a concise draft with three recommended reservation profiles and an activation cadence. Summary below and full details in pulsebridge-dedicated-options-v1.pdf + forecast spreadsheet.

Option A - Conservative (Low capex risk)
- Min GPUs: 8 (NVIDIA H32 equivalent)
- Target p99 latency: ~450-600ms (with batching optimized for 800-token avg)
- Activation: immediate for development + 60-day hold before production scale
- Ramp: add 8 GPUs every 8 weeks based on 10% sustained increase in p99 requests
- Pricing: blended reserved rate + modest overage (30% lower than on-demand)
- Use-case: extended pilot, strict commitment budget

Option B - Balanced (Recommended for target profile)
- Min GPUs: 32
- Target p99 latency: ~220-300ms
- Activation: 4-week staging -> production activation at week 5
- Ramp: structured 3-month ramp to 64 GPUs (milestones at month 1, month 2, month 3) tied to usage triggers in the SOW
- Pricing: tiered reserved pricing with burst pool and token caps; includes 50k tokens/day warm-up credits for initial model cache priming
- Use-case: expected production launch with room for growth — best tradeoff for latency and cost

Option C - Aggressive (Growth-first)
- Min GPUs: 64
- Target p99 latency: ~120-180ms
- Activation: 2-week staging -> production at week 3
- Ramp: immediate availability to scale to 128 GPUs within 6 weeks on committed run-rate
- Pricing: deeper reserved discount, higher minimum commitment, includes 200k tokens/day warm-up credits and a 14-day warm-start runway
- Use-case: high-growth product with strict latency SLOs and SLA financials

Operational notes / caveats:
- Lead time: baseline activation (first GPUs online) ~7 business days after PO signed; larger rack/firmware prep for >64 GPUs can add 10-15 business days. We will confirm exact dates against availability windows in the SOW.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to compatible model variants if capacity constrained; documented in the runbook.
- Escrow/SLA: standard enterprise SLA available (99.9% platform) with credits for sustained downtime; legal team will provide template redlines but names and timelines need alignment.

Attachments: pulsebridge-dedicated-options-v1.pdf (detailed scenarios), pulsebridge-forecast-token-profile.xlsx (expected token/day forecast per scenario).

Next steps:
1) Let us know which option you want to include in the SOW (or we can combine elements).
2) If Option B, confirm target production date and whether you want the 50k warm-up credits to be front-loaded across the first 30 days.
3) Procurement to send PO to procure@redwood.ai or we can accept DocuSign.

Happy to jump on a call to walk the spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

---
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@pulsebridge.ai>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-11T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PulseBridge - Dedicated reservation options (draft)

Thanks Ben — this is a great start. A couple quick additions from onboarding and ops perspective:

- Warm-up runbook: we recommend a 7-day staged KV warm-start followed by a 14-day prefix cache exercise for chat workloads; well include a checklist in the SOW and offer a one-time concierge run for the first 30 days.
- Activation triggers: define measurable signals (e.g., sustained 3-day moving avg > X p99 req/min or token/day thresholds). Tying ramp steps to those signals avoids manual escalations.
- Cost guardrails: propose a hard cap option for month 1 to avoid unexpected overages; we can implement alerts at 60/80/95% of daily token budget.
- Legal/Procurement: we prefer DocuSign for the PO and a single-sheet SOW that lists ramp milestones + lead times (reconciles with your timeline Ben).

Michael — would you like us to bake these into Option B (recommended), or would you prefer a separate annex with operational runbook?

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Onboarding, Redwood Inference

---
From: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@pulsebridge.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: PulseBridge - Dedicated reservation options (draft)

Team,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear options. PulseBridge is comfortable moving forward with Option B (Balanced) with the following asks before we sign:
1) Confirm lead time for initial 32 GPUs will be 7 business days after PO receipt.
2) Include the 50k tokens/day warm-up credits front-loaded across the first 30 days.
3) Add the hard cap and alerting guardrails Laura described for month 1.
4) Please attach a one-page SOW annexing ramp milestones and the warm-up runbook.

Ive attached a preliminary PO (PulseBridge_PO_43021.pdf) to start procurement intake — legal will follow with DocuSign once the SOW annex is finalized. Wed like to lock the activation window for the week of June 24 if possible.

If you can confirm the lead times and send the one-page annex today, procurement will issue the PO and we can proceed.

Appreciate everyone moving quickly here.

Best,
Michael
VP Engineering, PulseBridge
